key_insight: EdgeBench shows that agent performance from real-world environment learning follows a highly precise log-sigmoid scaling law, and learning speed has roughly doubled every three months across model generations.
engineering_relevance: This provides a quantitative basis for predicting and benchmarking how deployed agents improve from long-horizon interaction, informing evaluation, training, and deployment planning.
method: Built EdgeBench: 134 real-world tasks spanning scientific discovery, software engineering, optimization, knowledge work, math, and games
Ran agents for ultra-long horizons with rich multilevel feedback; each task lasts at least 12 continuous hours
Analyzed scaling behavior of performance and learning speed across roughly 38,000 hours of interaction
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analysis of about 38,000 hours of agent-environment interaction across 134 tasks, with overall performance following a log-sigmoid scaling law at R^2 = 0.998.
watch_item: Results are based on a curated benchmark with substantial expert construction effort, so generalization to all real-world deployments and feedback regimes may be limited.
paper_title: EdgeBench: Unveiling Scaling Laws of Learning from Real-World Environments
